2609.01274.title: From Base Rollouts to RL Reasoning: A Budgeted Search Perspective
2609.01274.paper_summary: Reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) improves language-model reasoning, but how these gains relate to inference-time decoding and search remains unclear. Does RL create reasoning the base model lacks, or shift the rollout distribution toward trajectories it can already reach but rarely samples? We study this behaviorally with a Unified Decoding Framework (UDF), which expresses token-level sampling, beam-like search, tree search, and sequence-level resampling as executable policies over a shared budgeted operating space, scored post hoc with pass@$k$, self-consistency, best-of-$N$, and first-finish success. Using paired Base/RL checkpoints from SimpleRL-Zoo, we ask whether an RL default-policy curve can be approximated by a structured path of Base operating points. On Math500, AIME, GPQA, and IFEval, the pass@$k$ recovery path follows a Budgeted Operating-Point Transition Rule (BOPTR), $N_{\mathrm{Base}} \approx αN_{\mathrm{RL}}^β$, with benchmark-conditioned exponents. On Qwen2.5-7B, BOPTR gives the lowest transfer error among the non-oracle rules we test, 3.41 pp (95% CI [2.32, 5.53]); a three-seed replication gives 3.07 $\pm$ 0.39 pp. The rule extends to ten models across four families (3.28 to 4.87 pp on checkpoints added after fitting), to four benchmarks it was never fitted on (5.03 pp vs. 4.44 pp in fit), and holds without an RL checkpoint for the target model (4.19 pp) or without RL supervision of any kind (5.08 pp). These results support a qualified internalized-search reading: under the recipe we test, much of the measured RL gain corresponds to a change in sampling efficiency toward operating points the base model can already reach under search. We treat the scaling patterns as descriptive of this recipe and cohort, report where they break down, and use UDF and BOPTR as behavioral diagnostics rather than evidence of parameter-level equivalence.
2609.01274.paper_summary_zh: 強化學習與可驗證獎勵（RLVR）改善了語言模型的推理，但這些增益與推理時間解碼和搜索之間的關係仍不清楚。RL是否創造了基礎模型所缺乏的推理，或者是否將展開分佈轉向它已經能夠到達但很少取樣的軌跡？我們通過統一解碼框架（UDF）行為上研究這一現象，該框架將令牌級取樣、類似束搜索、樹搜索和序列級重取樣表達為在共享預算操作空間上的可執行策略，並在事後用pass@$k$、自我一致性、最佳的$N$和首次完成成功進行評分。使用來自SimpleRL-Zoo的配對基礎/RL檢查點，我們詢問是否可以通過一條結構化的基礎操作點路徑來近似RL默認策略曲線。在Math500、AIME、GPQA和IFEval上，pass@$k$恢復路徑遵循預算操作點轉換規則（BOPTR），$N_{\mathrm{Base}} \approx αN_{\mathrm{RL}}^β$，具有基準條件的指數。在Qwen2.5-7B上，BOPTR在我們測試的非神諭規則中給出了最低的轉移誤差，為3.41個百分點（95% CI [2.32, 5.53]）；三次種子重複給出3.07 $\pm$ 0.39個百分點。該規則擴展到四個家族的十個模型（在擬合後添加的檢查點上為3.28到4.87個百分點），對於四個從未擬合的基準（擬合時為5.03個百分點對比4.44個百分點），並且在目標模型沒有RL檢查點的情況下（4.19個百分點）或沒有任何形式的RL監督的情況下（5.08個百分點）仍然成立。這些結果支持了一種合格的內部化搜索解讀：在我們測試的配方下，測量到的RL增益大部分對應於取樣效率向基礎模型在搜索中已經能夠到達的操作點的變化。我們將這些縮放模式視為對這一配方和群體的描述，報告它們何時失效，並使用UDF和BOPTR作為行為診斷，而不是參數級等價的證據。
